blogs.title: Who Gets the Penalty? The Eighth Circuit’s Strict Read of the MPWA
blogs.description: An analysis of the court's statutory interpretation of the Minnesota Payment of Wages Act. This post explores the distinction between an employee's right to 'prosecute a claim for wages' and the Commissioner's exclusive authority to collect 'average daily wage penalties,' discussing the 'legislature knows how' canon of construction used by the court to limit private recoveries.

blogs.title: Standing to Sue for the State: Civil Penalties and the Mootness Doctrine
blogs.description: This post examines the jurisdictional tension in the MFLSA claim: whether a plaintiff maintains Article III standing to pursue civil penalties that benefit the government after their own personal damages have been satisfied. It analyzes the application of the 'Friends of the Earth' doctrine and the 'voluntary cessation' exception in the context of ongoing corporate payroll policies.

blogs.title: Briefs Are Not Complaints: The Perils of Shifting Relief at Summary Judgment
blogs.description: A procedural cautionary tale focusing on the court's refusal to consider Cohen's request for an injunctive order to rescind a specific policy. This post discusses the boundaries of Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 15 and the dangers of attempting to alter the scope of requested relief through summary judgment briefing rather than formal complaint amendments.
